subject: MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmark plan & owners
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Emilia Torres <emilia@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmark plan & owners

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clarity on the primary success criteria for the HealthGrid proof-of-concept. Quick recap and proposed owners for the MAP technical evaluation milestone so we can lock dependencies and the target close date. Attaching a first-pass MAP draft and the benchmark workbook I mentioned.

Summary / asks from today's call:
- Goal: Validate model candidate that meets HealthGrid quality and ops SLOs for triage assistant (safety + recall).
- Success criteria (proposed):
  * Latency: p95 <= 200ms for 256–512 token responses in a reserved environment
  * Cost: infer cost <= $0.12 per 1k output tokens (target first-run)
  * Quality: automated BLEU/ROUGE baseline + human eval pass rate >= 85% on labelled sampling
  * Embeddings: recall@10 >= 0.88 on our retrieval eval set
- Model shortlist to evaluate (initial): Llama-3 34B (8-bit), Redwood-Open-7B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-8B

Proposed owners / milestone timeline:
- Benchmark harness & infra provisioning: Ben Carter (bench infra + scripts)
- Model profiling & hyperparam pass: Marissa Cole
- Customer stakeholder sync / MAP coordination / close: me (Karthik Iyer)
- Target close date for MAP milestone: 2027-04-22 (flexible — please flag conflicts)

Dependencies we flagged on the call:
- HealthGrid to deliver the de-identified evaluation dataset (schema + sample) by 2027-03-05
- Access to a dedicated sandbox (SOC2-friendly) for latency runs — we can provide instructions for on-prem / VPC options
- Agreement on scoring rubric for quality vs cost tradeoffs

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf, benchmark-suite.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Emilia, can you confirm dataset delivery ETA and whether the sandbox will be available?
2) Marissa/Ben — I'll schedule a 30-min sync next week to align infra pre-reqs.
3) I'll update the MAP document with the owners and deadline and send a single-line mutual action plan for signatures.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Emilia Torres <emilia@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthGrid Technical Evaluations <tech-evals@healthgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmark plan & owners

Thanks, Karthik — good capture. A few quick clarifications from our side: we can deliver a de-identified snapshot and the sampling instructions, target ETA 2027-03-04 (earlier if we prioritize). The sandbox: our infra team can spin a VPC peer for Redwood but it requires an approved compliance checklist (we'll share).

On the success criteria: the latency p95 target looks reasonable, but the cost target will depend on the final model config (quantization, batch size). We want the report to show cost/latency tradeoffs per model variant.

A couple of asks from HealthGrid:
- Please include a throughput target (QPS) for the benchmark runs — we need numbers for peak-hour sizing.
- Can you add an explicit human-eval plan (who runs it, how many samples) to the MAP? We prefer at least 500 labelled samples for the final pass.

Target close date is fine from our side if we keep the 2027-04-22 window. We will circulate the SOC2 checklist by EOD Mon (2027-03-01). I've attached the evaluation dataset bundle (healthgrid-eval-set.zip) to this reply.

Emilia Torres
Head of Integrations
HealthGrid
emilia@healthgrid.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation milestone — benchmark plan & owners

+1 on Karthik's recap and Emilia's asks. I've sketched an internal runbook and assigned first-pass tasks below so we can give HealthGrid a crisp start-of-work plan.

Concrete plan and owners:
- Week 1 (2027-03-08 to 2027-03-12): infra prep + data ingest (owner: Ben)  * Provision bench cluster (GPU nodes), baseline harness from benchmark-suite.xlsx  * Validate dataset load and sampling script against HealthGrid bundle
- Week 2 (2027-03-15 to 2027-03-19): model profiling (owner: Marissa)  * Run model variants at representative seq lengths (128/256/512)  * Measure latency p50/p95, memory, and KV cache behavior- Week 3 (2027-03-22 to 2027-03-26): quality passes + human eval prep (owner: Marissa + HealthGrid)  * Prepare 500-sample human-eval packet; define rubric and inter-rater agreement target- Week 4 (2027-03-29 to 2027-04-02): cost/throughput stress tests (owner: Ben)  * Run QPS scenarios, capture cost per 1k tokens estimates, and quantify batch sizing impacts- Week 5 (2027-04-05 to 2027-04-09): collate results and scoring (owner: Marissa + Karthik)  * Produce a results deck with cost/latency/quality tradeoff curves

Dependencies and blockers:
- SOC2 checklist & sandbox access (HealthGrid) — blocker for latency runs in dedicated environment
- Agreement on final model shortlist — we can expand after Week 1 but want to fix 3 candidates to reduce noise
Deliverables we will produce for the MAP milestone:
- Benchmark report (latency/cost/quality)- Raw logs + harness (drive link)- Human-eval scoring spreadsheet- Proposed model recommendation and rollout suggestion

I'll put times on calendars for a 30-min infra sync on Mon 2027-03-08 10:00am PT (Ben + Karthik + HealthGrid infra rep). Karthik — if that works, I'll include the drive link to the harness and the draft MAP (MAP-draft-v1.pdf).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
